verdicts.title: Recent advances on the log-rank conjecture in communication complexity
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The log-rank conjecture is one of the fundamental open problems in communication complexity. It speculates that the deterministic communication complexity of any two-party function is equal to the log of the rank of its associated matrix, up to polynomial factors. Despite much research, we still know very little about this conjecture. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract describes a survey on the log-rank conjecture in communication complexity, but does not mention Dyck-path zero-crossing counts or any row-walk statistic like R(f), so it neither supports nor refutes the specific √(rk·N·log N) bound proposed.

verdicts.title: The Log-Rank Conjecture: New Equivalent Formulations
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
The log-rank conjecture is a longstanding open problem with multiple equivalent formulations in complexity theory and mathematics. In its linear-algebraic form, it asserts that the rank and partitioning number of a Boolean matrix are quasi-polynomially related.

verdicts.title: An additive combinatorics approach to the log-rank conjecture in communication complexity
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: For a $\{0,1\}$-valued matrix $M$ let $\rm{CC}(M)$ denote the deterministic communication complexity of the boolean function associated with $M$. The log-rank conjecture of Lovász and Saks [FOCS 1988] states that $\rm{CC}(M) \leq \log^c(\rm{rank}(M))$ for some absolute constant $c$ where $\rm{rank}(M)$ denotes the rank of $M$ over the field of real numbers.
